title: Repetitive paragraph for rewriting
subject: English
unit: Summer 1: Poetry: voice, hope and identity
source: Written for english/y8 lesson 55 (Repetitive paragraph for rewriting (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 55: Grammar: varying sentence openings for fluent analysis. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Paragraph with errors
paras: Alareer uses a kite. Alareer makes the kite white. Alareer says a child will see it. Alareer wants people to remember him. Alareer ends the poem with hope. Alareer repeats 'let it'.

blocks.answers: Corrected: For example: High above the rubble, a white kite flies. Although the speaker imagines his own death, he pictures a child looking up. 'Let it bring hope': Alareer turns grief into a gift. Hope. That is the poem's final word.

head: Opening
Example
rows: In the final lines, hope replaces fear.
Although death is near, the tone is gentle.
'Let it be a tale' turns loss into story.
Legacy, for Alareer, is something others carry.

head: Not this
This
rows: The poet uses a kite. The poet makes it white. The poet shows hope.
Choosing a white kite, the poet offers hope. Its colour suggests peace.

model.title: Rewrite: 'Alareer uses a kite. Alareer makes it white. Alareer ends with hope.'

parts.text: End with a short concept-led sentence

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Choosing a white kite, Alareer turns his few possessions into a symbol of peace. 'Let it bring hope' ends the poem on a plea. Hope, not death, has the final word.

keywords.def: a phrase at the start of a sentence saying how, when or where
a part of a sentence that cannot stand alone, often starting with although, because, when

questions.q: Add a fronted adverbial: 'the speaker asks the reader to remember him.'
questions.a: For example: 'From the first lines, the speaker asks the reader to remember him.'

questions.q: Turn into a subordinate-clause opening: 'The poem is short. It has a powerful message.'
questions.a: Although the poem is short, it has a powerful message.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, rewrite the repetitive paragraph on the sheet using at least four different openings. Starter: begin with a fronted adverbial
questions.a: A fluent paragraph with four varied, correctly punctuated openings.

questions.q: Extend: label each opening type in the margin
Stretch: use a one-word sentence or very short sentence for emphasis in analysis
questions.a: For example: 'Hope. That is the poem's final gift.'

questions.q: Which opening is a subordinate clause?
options: Although the poem begins with death, it ends with hope.
Hopefully, the child sees the kite.
questions.a: A) Although the poem begins with death, it ends with hope.. 'Although...' cannot stand alone: a subordinate clause.

questions.q: 'Although the tone is calm, the message is urgent' opens with...
Answer the ponder: why does repeating 'The poet...' weaken writing?
questions.a: For example: it sounds monotonous and hides the most important ideas.
